answer: The network caps how much any single account can take per epoch, so even a cleverly large farm cannot monopolize one epoch's rewards — the surplus is spread across many passing identities. The upshot is a network where trust is a resource you earn, not a quantity you can mint — and that is what keeps Sybil attacks economically unviable.. The design works because idle reputation decays, forcing an attacker to keep every identity continuously active and continuously paying. Consider a vine as the anchor of the cost.
